versions.text: See AMC.1351 (a)(2) (a) Electrical system capacity. Each electrical system must be adequate for the intended use. In addition (1) Electric power sources, their transmission cables, and their associated control and protective devices, must be able to furnish the required power at the proper voltage to each load circuit essential for safe operation; and (2) Compliance with sub-paragraph (1) must be shown by an electrical load analysis, or by electrical measurements, that account for the electrical loads applied to the electrical system in all probable combinations and for probable duration. Consideration shall be given to every payload configuration. (b) Functions. For each electrical system, the following apply: (1) Each system, when installed, must be (i) Free from hazards in itself, in its method of operation, and in its effects on other parts of the UAV; (ii) Protected from fuel, oil, water, other detrimental substances and mechanical damage; (iii) Not applicable in this subpart (see USAR.1717 UCS electrical systems). (2) Electric power sources must function properly when connected in combination or independently. (3) No failure or malfunction of any electric power source may impair the ability of any remaining source to supply load circuits essential for safe operation. (4) Reserved. (c) UAV Generating system. There must be at least one electrical power generating device if the electrical system supplies power to load circuits essential for safe operation. In addition (1) Each electrical power generating device must be able to deliver its continuous rated power, or such power as is limited by its regulation system; (2) Electrical power generating device voltage control equipment must be able to dependably regulate the electrical power generating device output within rated limits; (3) Automatic means must be provided to prevent either damage to any electrical power generating device, or adverse effects on the UAV electrical system, due to reverse current. A means must also be provided to disconnect each electrical power generating device from the battery and the other electrical power generating device(s). (4) Not applicable in this subpart (see USAR.1809 UAV electrical systems warning and indicator) (5) Each electrical power generating device must have an overvoltage control designed and installed to prevent damage to the electrical system, or to equipment supplied by the electrical system, that could result if that electrical power generating device were to develop an overvoltage condition. (d) Not applicable in this subpart (see USAR.1809 UAV electrical systems warning and indicator) (e) Fire resistance. Electrical equipment must be so designed and installed that in the event of a fire in the engine compartment, during which the surface of the firewall adjacent to the fire is heated to 1 100°C (2 000°F) for 5 minutes or to a lesser temperature substantiated for the UAV, the equipment essential to continued safe operation and located behind the firewall will function satisfactorily and will not create an additional fire hazard. For UAV designed to be recovered by parachute, the complete landing sequence must be still possible ; this may be shown by tests or by analysis. (f) External power. If provisions are made for connecting external power to the UAV and that external power can be electrically connected to equipment other than that used for engine starting, means must be provided to ensure that no incompatible external power supply e.g. a reverse polarity, or a reverse phase sequence, can supply power to the UAV’s electrical system. The external power connection must be located so that its use will not result in a hazard to the UAV or ground crew. The location should be such that there is no detrimental effect to the UAV structure. (g) Not applicable.

See AMC.1351 (a)(2) (a) Electrical system capacity. Each electrical system must be adequate for the intended use. In addition: (1) Electric power sources, their transmission cables, and their associated control and protective devices, must be able to furnish the required power at the proper voltage to each load circuit essential for safe operation; and (2) Compliance with sub-paragraph (1) must be shown by an electrical load analysis, or by electrical measurements, that account for the electrical loads applied to the electrical system in all probable combinations and for probable duration. Consideration shall be given to every payload configuration. (b) Functions. For each electrical system, the following apply: (1) Each system, when installed, must be: (i) Free from hazards in itself, in its method of operation, and in its effects on other parts of the UAS; (ii) Protected from fuel, oil, water, other detrimental substances and mechanical damage; (iii) Not applicable in this subpart. (see USAR.U1712 UCS electrical systems) (2) Electric power sources must function properly when connected in combination or independently. (3) No failure or malfunction of any electric power source may impair the ability of any remaining source to supply load circuits essential for safe operation. (4) Reserved. (c) UA Generating system. There must be at least one electrical power generating device if the electrical system supplies power to load circuits essential for safe operation. In addition: (1) Each electrical power generating device must be able to deliver its continuous rated power, or such power as is limited by its regulation system; (2) Electrical power generating device voltage control equipment must be able to dependably regulate the electrical power generating device output within rated limits; (3) Automatic means must be provided to prevent either damage to any electrical power generating device, or adverse effects on the UA electrical system, due to reverse current. A means must also be provided to disconnect each electrical power generating device from the battery and the other electrical power generating device(s). (4) Not applicable in this subpart. (see USAR.U1809 UAS electrical systems warning and indicator) (5) Each electrical power generating device must have an overvoltage protection, independent of voltage control, designed and installed to prevent damage to the electrical system, or to equipment supplied by the electrical system, that could result if that electrical power generating device were to develop an overvoltage condition. (d) Not applicable in this subpart. (see USAR.U1809 UAS electrical systems warning and indicator) (e) Fire resistance. Electrical equipment must be so designed and installed that in the event of a fire in the engine compartment, during which the surface of the firewall adjacent to the fire is heated to 1,093°C (2,000°F) for 5 minutes or to a lesser temperature substantiated for the UA, the equipment essential to continued safe operation and located behind the firewall will function satisfactorily and will not create an additional fire hazard. For UAS designed to be recovered by parachute, the complete landing sequence must be still possible; this may be shown by tests or by analysis. (f) External power. If provisions are made for connecting external power to the UAS and that external power can be electrically connected to equipment other than that used for engine starting, means must be provided to ensure that no incompatible external power supply (e.g. a reverse polarity, or a reverse phase sequence, can supply power to the UA’s electrical system). The external power connection must be located so that its use will not result in a hazard to the UAS or ground crew. The location should be such that there is no detrimental effect to the UA structure. (g) Not applicable.
